title: Rebates Allowed on a Catering Cancellation Charge Where the Agreement Trades Well
content:
A rebate is taken off the cancellation charge raised on a Corporate Catering Service Agreement where the agreement has been delivering regularly and the pulled order was a substantial one.

1. **Where the agreement carried 6 or more deliveries in the 12 months ending on the day notice is given and the value the cancellation entry carries reaches twice — 2 times — the minimum order value printed against the catering service level**, a rebate of 30 per cent of the charge is allowed.
2. **Where the agreement carried at least 3 but fewer than 6 deliveries in those 12 months and the value the cancellation entry carries reaches the minimum order value printed against the catering service level**, a rebate of 15 per cent is allowed.
3. **Otherwise**, no rebate is allowed.

### Both sides of the counts and the values

Take a hypothetical agreement whose catering service level is printed with a minimum order value of 480.00 USD, so that twice that value is 960.00 USD.

| Deliveries in the 12 months ending on the day notice is given | Value the cancellation entry carries | Rebate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7 | 1200.00 USD | 30 per cent |
| 6 | 960.00 USD | 30 per cent |
| 6 | 959.99 USD | none |
| 5 | 1200.00 USD | 15 per cent |
| 3 | 480.00 USD | 15 per cent |
| 3 | 479.99 USD | none |
| 2 | 2000.00 USD | none |

A delivery record of 6 or more that does not reach twice the minimum order value meets neither branch: the second branch is written for a record of at least 3 and fewer than 6, so a record of 6 does not fall back onto it. The rebate is a percentage of the charge, not of the value the cancellation entry carries: on a charge of 300.00 USD a rebate of 30 per cent is 90.00 USD, leaving 210.00 USD.
